title: The most absurd records
text: Not every world record is about being the fastest or the strongest. Some of the records in the Guinness book are so absurd that you might laugh when you read them. But each one has required hours of effort.

Have you ever tried to balance a spoon on your nose? A man from Iran has balanced thirty-one spoons on his face at the same time. Another person has kept a pencil balanced on his nose for more than eleven minutes.

Food records are also popular. People have built the largest pizza, the longest sandwich and the tallest cake. A team in Italy has made a pizza more than one thousand eight hundred meters long. After the record, the pizza was shared with everyone.
Some records involve animals. A dog called Purin has caught more balls with its paws than any other dog in one minute. And a cat called Didga has done more tricks on a skateboard than any other cat.

Why do people do it? Many say they have always dreamed of seeing their name in the book. Others just enjoy the challenge. Since the book first appeared in 1955, millions of people have tried to break a record. Have you ever thought about it?

grammar.title: Grammar: the present perfect
grammar.rule: Use the present perfect (have / has + past participle) for experiences and for past actions without a specific time. Use ever in questions and never for negative experiences.
rows: make → made, do → done, see → seen
items: ___ you ever tried to break a record?
I have ___ seen a cat on a skateboard.
The dog has ___ more balls than any other dog.
